chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When you pray and you are facing away from the Qibla, and it becomes clear to you that you are facing away from the Qibla, and you are within the time [of the prayer], then repeat [the prayer]; and if the time has passed for you, then do not repeat."

key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The direction of prayer (towards the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.فِي وَقْتٍ: Within the prescribed time of the prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if I realize I was facing the wrong direction during prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between two scenarios based on the timing of the realization: if the error is noticed within the prayer's specific time window, the prayer must be repeated (qada' or fada' depending on interpretation, but here implying re-praying within the time); if the time has expired, the original prayer suffices. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of obligatory prayers is tied to their prescribed times, offering practical clarity for worshippers who may face uncertainty during prayer.
